'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[Afghan peace process]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] says that he [[2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan|plans to withdraw]] all remaining American troops in [[Afghanistan]] by September 11. The United States also reiterates its support for the [[Afghan government]] against the [[Taliban]], which declines to comment on the apparent change from the previously-agreed deadline of May 1. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-afghanistan-withdrawal/biden-set-to-withdraw-u-s-troops-from-afghanistan-by-sept-11-idUSKBN2C028S?il=0 (Reuters)]
***The [[United Kingdom]] announces that it will withdraw nearly all of its [[British Armed Forces|troops]] from Afghanistan, following the announcement of a U.S. withdrawal. There are around 750 British soldiers still stationed in Afghanistan, mostly in the capital [[Kabul]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-afghanistan-withdrawal-britain/britain-to-withdraw-nearly-all-its-troops-from-afghanistan-the-times-idUSKBN2C02Y1?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[Turkey]] says that it will host a summit from April 24 to May 4 in an effort to end the [[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|war]] in [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/13/turkey-to-host-10-day-afghan-taliban-peace-talks-from-april-24 (Al Jazeera)]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A [[car bomb]]ing in [[Farah, Afghanistan|Farah]] kills three civilians; and 10 security personnel are killed in the country's north. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/car-bomb-kills-afghanistan-10-troops-killed-north-77049191 (ABC News)]
*[[Iran–Israel proxy conflict]]
**A missile strikes the [[Israel]]i-owned  [[cargo ship]] MV ''Hyperion Ray'' off the coast of the [[United Arab Emirates]]. There is no immediate claim of responsibility, however Israeli officials suspect [[Iran]] of being behind the attack on the vessel. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israeli-owned-ship-said-attacked-off-uae-coast-amid-sky-high-tensions-with-iran/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[Terrorism in Pakistan]], [[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**An [[improvised explosive device]] explodes at a [[association football|football]] ground in [[Hub, Balochistan|Hub]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]], injuring twelve people. The attack occurred during a game organised as a commemorative tribute to police officers killed in the line of duty. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/explosion-rocks-football-ground-during-match-in-pakistan-12-injured/articleshow/82055034.cms (''The Times of India'')]
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**''[[The New York Times]]'' says that a blackout at [[Iran]]'s underground [[Natanz]] nuclear facility was [[sabotage]] perpetrated by remotely detonating an [[improvised explosive device]] that had previously been smuggled into the site. [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/international/middle-east/1618290789-report-explosive-device-smuggled-into-natanz-plant-remotely-detonated (i24news)]
*A [[military court]] in [[Burkina Faso]] indicts (''[[trial in absentia|in absentia]]'') ex-President [[Blaise Compaoré]], who is charged with the 1987 murder of his immediate predecessor [[Thomas Sankara]]. Compaoré ruled the nation for 27 years following Sankara's assassination before resigning in the face of protests in 2014 and fleeing into exile in [[Ivory Coast]]. The court indicts thirteen other Burkinabé ex-officials accused of various crimes including murder. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/13/burkina-faso-ex-president-blaise-compaore-charged-thomas-sankara-murder (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]], [[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
**Talks between rail workers and [[Abellio ScotRail|ScotRail]] aimed at preventing a [[Strike action|strike]] collapse, as the rail firm cites [[economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic|financial pressures caused by the ongoing pandemic]] to justify refusing a pay raise and revocation of some day-off entitlements. The [[Unite the Union|Unite]] union rejects this explanation. The [[Scottish Government]] and [[Transport Scotland]] are appraised of the situation. [https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/19229399.scotrail-strike-edges-closer-pay-talks-collapse/ (''The Glasgow Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Discharge of radioactive water of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]]
**Following a [[Cabinet of Japan|cabinet]] meeting, the Japanese government says it has decided to release 1.25 million tons of treated [[Radioactive contamination|radioactive]] water from the crippled [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]] into the [[Pacific Ocean]] over the course of 30 years, after concluding there will be no negative impact on human health or the environment. The decision is opposed by Russia, China, Taiwan, South Korea, North Korea and the Philippines, while being supported by the United States. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/04/3b41a07d2e30-update1-japan-decides-to-release-water-from-fukushima-nuclear-plant-into-sea.html (Kyodo News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-56728068 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-disaster-fukushima-water-reaction/countries-react-to-japans-plans-to-release-fukushima-water-into-ocean-idUSKBN2C00WF?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Suez Canal obstruction]]
**A [[Judiciary of Egypt#Courts|court]] in [[Ismailia]] grants the [[Egypt]]ian [[Suez Canal Authority]]'s [[2021 Suez Canal obstruction#legal|request to seize]] [[ship prefix#usage|CS]] ''[[Ever Given]]'' pending payment of a compensation claim of over [[US$]]900 million. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-13/egypt-seizes-ever-given-pending-900m-compensation (Bloomberg)]
*[[2019 Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress crash]]
**The [[National Transportation Safety Board]] concludes that [[pilot error]] and inadequate maintenance were behind the crash, which killed seven people, injured six others, and destroyed the historic aircraft. [https://www.ctpost.com/news/article/NTSB-Pilot-s-actions-maintenance-issues-16098161.php (''The Connecticut Post'')]
*At least 20 children are killed during a fire at an school in [[Niamey]], [[Niger]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/14/niger-mourns-death-of-20-children-in-school-blaze (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****Iran reports a record 24,760 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,118,212. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1842221/middle-east (Arab News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Osaka Prefecture]] reports a record 1,099 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/04/13/national/daily-coronavirus-cases/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Syria]]
****Kurdish authorities impose a ten-day curfew in northeast Syria after a rapid increase of cases of COVID-19 in the region. The U.S.-backed Kurdish authorities also close all borders of its [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] territories with those controlled by the government and insurgent groups. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-middle-east-coronavirus-pandemic-496be724709bd136c00ede6f3867c115 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
****[[Prime Minister of France|Prime Minister]] [[Jean Castex]] announces the suspension of flights from [[Brazil]] in order to prevent the spread of new variants of COVID-19 in the country. [https://www.yahoo.com/news/france-suspends-flights-brazil-due-142156762.html (Yahoo! News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[President of Cantabria]] [[Miguel Ángel Revilla]] receives his first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.abc.es/espana/abci-revilla-recibe-vacuna-contra-covid-202104131257_video.html (ABC.es)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] announces a two-week partial [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] across [[Turkey]] on [[Ramadan]], which includes an expanded curfew from 7:00 p.m. and a ban on non-essential inter-city travel beginning tomorrow evening due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/turkey/turkey-declares-partial-lockdown-during-ramadan/2207946 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Central African Republic]]
****The first batch of [[AstraZeneca]] COVID-19 vaccines arrive in the [[Central African Republic]], with the [[MINUSCA]] [[United Nations peacekeeping|mission]] agency staff being the first recipients. [https://www.africanews.com/2021/04/15/c-a-r-receives-first-batch-of-covid-19-jabs-for-un-personnel-families/ (Africanews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****[[South Africa]] voluntarily suspends its rollout of the [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|Johnson & Johnson]] [[vaccine]] after the U.S. [[Food and Drug Administration]] recommended temporarily suspending use of the vaccine due to rare cases of [[blood clot]]s. [https://businesstech.co.za/news/trending/482897/south-africa-suspends-rollout-of-johnson-johnson-covid-vaccine/ (Business Tech)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Sudan]]
****[[President of South Sudan|South Sudan President]] [[Salva Kiir Mayardit]] receives his first dose of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|AstraZenaca vaccine]]. [https://allafrica.com/stories/202104140724.html (AllAfrica)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[United States]] suspends the use of the [[Johnson & Johnson]] [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] following concerns of [[Post-vaccination embolic and thrombotic events|blood clot]]s. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/13/us/politics/johnson-johnson-vaccine-blood-clots-fda-cdc.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] reports a record 27,001 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,578,946. [https://www.pagina12.com.ar/335431-otro-record-se-registraron-27-001-nuevos-casos-de-coronaviru (''Página 12'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Marshall Islands]]
***The [[Marshall Islands]] reaches an adult population vaccination rate of nearly 75%. After completing the urban areas, the Ministry of Health and Human Services plans to distribute [[Moderna]] and [[Johnson & Johnson]] vaccines to the most remote islands of the country to vaccinate the rest of the population. The vaccines were provided as a donation by the [[United States]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/440391/three-quarters-of-urban-marshall-islanders-get-first-covid-jab (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]], [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
***[[Moderna]] says its [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] is 90% effective against COVID-19, and 95% effective against severe disease for six months after the second dose. It also says its vaccine is effective against the [[501.V2 variant]] from [[South Africa]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/04/13/covid-vaccine-moderna-says-new-data-shows-its-90percent-effective-six-months-after-second-dose.html (CNBC)] [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/vaccine-made-for-south-african-covid-variant-promising-says-moderna-xz6hmzmt3 (The Times)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Terrorism in Germany]]
**[[2020 Dresden knife attack]]
***An alleged [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] recruiter goes on trial for stabbing two gay men in [[Dresden]], killing one of them, because they were holding hands. The suspect has admitted to the attack and is charged with [[murder]] and [[attempted murder]]. [https://www.pinknews.co.uk/2021/04/13/dresden-knife-attack-isis-stabbing-murder-abdullah-ahh-gay-men-thomas-oliver-l/ (Pink News)]
**Eleven alleged members of [[Gruppe S]], an alleged [[far-right terror]] [[clandestine cell system|cell]] plotting anti-[[immigration to Germany|immigration]] attacks, go on trial in [[Stuttgart]]. A policeman accused of assisting the group also goes on trial. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-56716712 (BBC News)]
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]], [[Daunte Wright protests]]
**Protests spread across the country over the police killing of [[Killing of Daunte Wright|Daunte Wright]]. Demonstrations and marches are held in [[New York City|New York]], [[Los Angeles]], [[Seattle]], [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]], and other cities. [https://www.npr.org/2021/04/13/986764183/protests-grow-in-minnesota-and-around-u-s-over-death-of-daunte-wright (NPR)]
*[[Terrorism in England]], [[Crime in London]]
**A court sentences terror convict Sahayb Abu to [[life imprisonment in England and Wales|life imprisonment]] with a [[Life imprisonment in England and Wales#Minimum term|minimum term]] of nineteen years for plotting a gun and knife attack in [[Dagenham]], [[London]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-56697609 (BBC News)]
*[[St Paul's Cathedral bomb plot]], [[Terrorism in Norway]]
**Authorities in [[Norway]] charge a man with involvement in a plot to bomb [[St Paul's Cathedral]] as well as plotting a similar attack in Norway. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-56729605 (BBC News)]
